title: Yankees’ historic 13-run third inning powers wild win over A’s
content:
The New York Yankees became the first American League team in history to explode for 13 runs in an inning and zero for the rest of the game when they dropped the Athletics, 13-8, on Sunday afternoon in Sacramento.

The 13 runs in a single frame was one shy of the franchise record set in 1920. The Yankees had scored 13 runs in an inning twice before — both times during the 2005 season.

The Chicago White Stockings scored the most runs ever in one inning, plating 18 in the seventh inning of a 26-6 victory over the Detroit Wolverines on Sept. 6, 1883.

“Today was one of those crazy games that I don’t know what it was,” manager Aaron Boone told reporters, “but it was a win.”

The Yankees’ first 12 batters reached base in the inning, tying the longest streak in MLB since 1961, according to the YES Network.

Right fielder Aaron Judge said he had “never” experienced an inning like that, one in which the Yankees batted around twice and Anthony Volpe was left waiting on the on-deck circle for what would have been his third at-bat.

The Yankees’ 18 third-inning plate appearances were the most in franchise history since 1987. They faced three different pitchers (Jacob Lopez, Michael Kelly, Jack Perkins) and 75 total pitches in the inning, which lasted 43 minutes and necessitated starting pitcher Will Warren making the rare move of going to the bullpen to warm up mid-frame.

For his part, Warren didn’t allow an earned run over six innings, striking out five, walking three and giving up six hits. He improved to 7-1 with a 3.22 ERA.

The Yankees recorded 11 hits, walked four times and stole four bases in the third. They didn’t hit a single home run. The Yankees actually had just one baserunner the rest of the game — a sixth-inning Cody Bellinger walk.

In the third, Volpe, Ben Rice and Bellinger each recorded two hits. Rice doubled and tripled, driving in four runs and scoring two of his own. Volpe scored twice and stole two bases. Max Schuemann walked and had a two-run double. Austin Wells walked twice. Judge went 1-for-2 with an RBI single.

“Glad we were able to make it stand up,” Boone said. “Obviously, a lot of really good things offensively in that inning.”

The Yankees entered the third inning down, 3-0. They had been retired in order in each of the first two innings. With two outs in the first inning, center fielder Trent Grisham appeared to lose Jonah Heim’s high fly ball to shallow center in the sun and it hit his glove, allowing two runs to score. An RBI single from Lawrence Butler came in the next at-bat.

Before the start of the third inning, Judge said he implored his teammates in the dugout to bring some energy.

“I thought we were a little asleep during those first two innings and I expect more out of the guys,” he said. “I know they expect more out of themselves. So, a couple of choice words there just to get it going, and the boys responded.”

The A’s didn’t back down, though.

They scored four runs in the seventh inning and another in the eighth to make it 13-8 going into the ninth. Closer David Bednar, who hadn’t pitched since Monday, then allowed a walk and a single with one out before finishing off the frame unblemished.

The win was the Yankees’ fifth of their six-game road trip, which included a three-game sweep in Kansas City. They’re in second place in the AL East, trailing the Tampa Bay Rays by 1 1/2 games. They have an off day Monday and begin a series against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.

“It (was) a really good trip,” Boone said. “So, you take that. I feel like for the most part we played well.”
